data.narrative:
Interlune is a seed-stage Space & Aerospace company founded by Rob Meyerson, Gary Lai, and Harrison Schmitt that has raised $23M to date. The sector comparison universe includes 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private companies, though direct comparables at Interlune's stage and scale remain limited.

Standard valuation triangulation methods encounter material constraints. Peer-median analysis is inapplicable: while 14 same-sector peers exist, zero qualify at Interlune's stage, adjacent stages, or similar valuation tier—the minimum threshold for reliable peer-median work is three datapoints. Public-comp anchoring, though the Space & Aerospace sector trades at a median 27.4x P/S across the six public tickers noted, cannot be executed without Interlune's revenue, which private companies typically do not disclose. The top private peers (SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, Planet Labs) serve as directional reference points only, as their historical valuations at comparable stages remain either proprietary or materially influenced by subsequent fundraising.

Given these constraints, a reliable quantitative valuation range cannot be synthesized from the available data. Further diligence would require: (1) revenue or unit economics disclosures from Interlune; (2) historical Series Seed valuations for at least three peer companies; or (3) explicit financing terms from recent SAFE instruments. Without these inputs, qualitative assessment of team, technology differentiation, and capital efficiency against known peers represents the only defensible analytical path.
